domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers the identification and analysis of prospective donors. It focuses on the methods used to research donor capacity and interest to support organizational fundraising goals and long-term development success.

This domain addresses the practical steps required to secure philanthropic gifts. It involves understanding the solicitation process and the techniques used to convert prospects into active donors for the organization.

This domain emphasizes the long-term cultivation of donor relationships. It covers strategies for maintaining engagement and ensuring donors feel connected to the organization's mission over time through consistent and meaningful communication.

This domain focuses on the integration of volunteers into fundraising activities. It examines how to effectively involve and manage volunteers to enhance organizational outreach and support for various development initiatives.

This domain covers the management of fundraising departments and leadership responsibilities. It includes organizational planning, resource allocation, and the oversight of development operations to ensure the success of the organization.

This domain addresses the ethical obligations and professional accountability of fundraisers. It covers legal compliance, transparency, and the management of conflicts of interest in philanthropic work to maintain high standards.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: The exam is a 240-minute session consisting of 200 questions. Ensure you arrive prepared to manage your time across all domains. Read each question carefully, focusing on the ethical and legal implications of the scenarios presented to ensure accuracy.

faq.answer_text: The CFRE exam consists of 200 questions that cover the defined domains of fundraising practice, requiring candidates to demonstrate their professional knowledge and application of various development principles throughout the assessment.
faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?

faq.answer_text: Candidates must achieve a score of 500 or above to pass the CFRE certification exam, which validates their expertise and commitment to the highest standards within the fundraising profession.
The exam has a total duration of 240 minutes, providing candidates with sufficient time to carefully review and answer all questions related to the core fundraising domains tested during the session.

For information regarding the long-term certification path or updates to requirements, please check with CFRE International for the current certification path, as they provide the most accurate and current details for all candidates.

editorial.overview: The Certified Fund Raising Executive (CFRE) certification, managed by CFRE International, validates professional fundraising expertise. The exam covers domains including donor research, gift securing, relationship building, volunteer involvement, leadership, and ethics. It assesses a candidate's ability to manage philanthropic programs, maintain donor relationships, and adhere to professional standards. This certification is intended for experienced professionals seeking to demonstrate their proficiency in the fundraising field through a standardized testing process that confirms their commitment to excellence in the nonprofit sector.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the domains to understand the weight of each topic. Focus on the ethical standards and professional requirements provided in the official documentation. Practice applying these rules to scenarios involving donor acknowledgments and contributions. Use the provided official exam guide to align your study habits with the structure of the 200-question assessment. Ensure you are familiar with all core concepts to succeed on the exam.
editorial.who_should_take: This exam is for fundraising professionals with practical experience in nonprofit development. Candidates should possess a background in managing donor relations, securing philanthropic gifts, and overseeing organizational leadership, as the exam tests real-world application of fundraising principles and ethical standards.
